texts: In AVSD the left-sided papillary muscles are located in the same vertical plane: C.

Because the common valve lacks the normal mitral arrangement, the left ventricular papillary muscles are rotated counterclockwise, one superior and one inferior, rather than anterolateral and posteromedial.
This crowds the left-sided valve's tension apparatus and must be respected when the left valve is reconstructed.
The Rastelli classification grades the bridging and attachments of the superior bridging leaflet, and type A, with the leaflet attached to the septal crest, is the most common.
In the picture, the two red pillars of the left engine room stand one above the other in an upright line.
Memory hook: in the shared-door hotel, the left pillars stand one above the other.
